strategy.summary: Reproduce astropy PR 20229 by building the source tree at buggy commit bdd570d53507, applying the developer's new parametrized tests in astropy/coordinates/tests/test_formatting.py, and running only those tests. The seconds-carry cases (e.g. Angle('1d2m59.49999s').to_string(precision=0)) and the fields=1 double-rounding cases (e.g. Angle('285d29m41.76s').to_string(fields=1)) should fail on the buggy revision and pass on the fixed one. Installing from PyPI with 'pip install astropy' is not sufficient, because released wheels already contain the fix. The dependency constraint is unbounded: the evidence gives no documented or era-based version bound for astropy, numpy or Python, so this plan chooses the versions the buggy source tree's own build configuration accepts and says so here.

build_commands: git clone https://github.com/astropy/astropy && cd astropy && git checkout bdd570d53507
pinned_because: Buggy revision bdd570d53507 is pinned by source checkout, not by a version number: the evidence gives the commit hash but no release or PR date, so the pre-fix behaviour must come from building that exact commit.
PyPI 'pip install astropy' is not used for reproduction because released versions post-date the fix and would pass the test without any transition.

No documented version constraint exists for astropy, numpy or Python in the evidence (documented_constraint null, era_ceiling null), so no numeric version pin is asserted; Python and numpy are whatever the buggy tree's build metadata accepts.
Build dependencies (cython, extension-helpers, setuptools_scm) are inferred from astropy's standard source build, not from the evidence; they are listed so that the editable build succeeds.

strategy.reproducing_test: astropy/coordinates/tests/test_formatting.py::test_sexagesimal_seconds_round_at_half_a_unit and test_sexagesimal_degrees_round_once (parametrized), as added by the developer's diff
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision bdd570d53507 with the test diff applied, the test run fails: the cases '1d2m59.49999s' at precision 0 (expects '1d02m59s', buggy gives '1d03m00s') and '285d29m41.76s' at fields=1 (expects '285d', buggy gives '286d') produce assertion failures. On the fixed revision (the merged commit of PR 20229), the same test run passes all parametrized cases with no failures.
risks: Only the source build at bdd570d53507 reproduces the defect; a PyPI install of any released astropy contains the fix and will show a pass on both sides, so no transition occurs.
The fixed revision's commit hash is not in the evidence; the fixed side must be taken as the merge of PR 20229, which should be confirmed against the PR page.

Tie cases such as '1d2m59.5s' and '1d59m59.5s' sit exactly on a half-unit boundary; builtin round versus NumPy round can differ on ties, so these cases depend on the implementation the fixed code uses and are a possible source of divergence across Python or numpy builds.
Double rounding appears only for fields=1 near the half-degree boundary; the test cases cover it, but no other field settings are evidenced to reproduce it.
No dtype or floating-point width is stated, so the reproduction assumes default float64 behaviour; a platform or float width that changes intermediate rounding is not confirmed by the evidence.
No platform, architecture or sanitiser requirement is stated in the evidence, so none is assumed; if the defect were architecture-specific it would not transition on a standard x86_64 Linux build.

oracle.reference_source: Expected strings given in the developer's test diff and the changelog
oracle.why: Angle.to_string returns a formatted string, so the check is exact string equality against the expected sexagesimal output; no numerical tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On bdd570d53507 the assertion Angle(...).to_string(...) == expected sees '1d03m00s' where '1d02m59s' is expected (seconds carried one step early), and '286d' where '285d' is expected (seconds rounded into minutes before minutes into degrees). The string comparison fails, so pytest reports these parametrized cases as failed.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the formatting uses round(float(values[2]), ndp) for fields == 3 and corrects the carry order, so every parametrized case returns the expected string and the test run passes.
